subject: POC mid-trial: scope sift, MOP evaluation plan and ownership
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@azuratech.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@azuratech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: POC mid-trial: scope sift, MOP evaluation plan and ownership

Alex / team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have a clear rebaseline for the trial if you decide to proceed with the additional intents we discussed.

Summary of proposed scope changes
- Add two secondary intents to the POC: Refund Extraction (structured fields) and Order Reroute (routing intent for customer service). These will be exercised on a 10% random sample of production-like transcripts.
- Keep core NLU + re-ranking evaluation on existing chat dataset (50k turns).

Proposed Measures of Performance (MOPs) — draft
- Refund Extraction: Precision >= 88% and Recall >= 82% on labeled evaluation set
- Order Reroute: Intent accuracy >= 90% and end-to-end successful handoff rate >= 93%
- Latency: P95 per-token generation < 220ms on Dedicated profile
- Cost impact: incremental token cost delta <= 12% vs baseline config

Timeline & ownership
- Confirm scope change and sign amendment: target by 2026-10-12 (Alex / Procurement)
- Redwood to deliver updated eval harness and synthetic labeling script: 2026-10-14 (Ben)
- Azura to provide 4 weeks of sample transcripts + labeled dev set (10k rows): 2026-10-21 (Alex)
- Joint evaluation window: 2026-10-22 to 2026-11-05

Attachments: updated MOP spreadsheet (redwood-updated-mop.xlsx) and a short draft amendment (link below).

Questions / asks for you today
1) Can Procurement confirm whether Azura is comfortable with the 10k labeled dev set ask? If not, what size is feasible?
2) Are the proposed thresholds acceptable as-is, or do you want to negotiate any of the MOPs (esp. recall for Refund Extraction)?
3) Please confirm sign-off cadence — if you can sign by 10/12 we can keep the current trial window, otherwise we should agree a new milestone.

I can hop on a 20-min call with Alex + Procurement tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Thanks —
Monica
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Rivera <alex@azuratech.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@azuratech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC mid-trial: scope sift, MOP evaluation plan and ownership

Thanks Monica — appreciate the clear write-up. Azura is broadly aligned but a couple of constraints from our side before we sign: 

1) Sample / labeling: 10k labeled rows is aggressive for our team this quarter. We can commit to 5k labeled rows within the same window if Redwood can (a) allow stratified sampling and (b) provide a lightweight labeling UI so our SMEs move faster.

2) Acceptance thresholds: We can accept the proposed Order Reroute accuracy target, but for Refund Extraction we need recall >= 78% (vs your 82%) given noise in historical transcripts. If Redwood can show a plan to iterate recall by +4 points during the rollout (i.e., staged acceptance and grooming), Procurement is ok with a slightly lower initial recall.

3) Timeline: Procurement has a cadence constraint — they need one extra week to route legal on the amendment. So signing slips to 2026-10-19. That would push the data delivery to 2026-10-28 and the joint evaluation window to 2026-10-29 -> 2026-11-12.

I've attached our SOC2 answers for your security team (azura-soc2-answers.pdf). Happy to run a short working session next week to align on labeling and the stratified sampling plan.

— Alex
Head of Product
Azura Tech
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <azuratech.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@azuratech.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC mid-trial: scope sift, MOP evaluation plan and ownership

Alex — thanks for the quick read and the SOC2 packet. Summary of Redwood's stance and proposed compromise below (copied Monica so this lives in thread):

1) Labels & tooling: We can provide a lightweight labeling UI and a stratified sampling script. That gets us to an effective 8k-equivalent labeled coverage given SME velocity. Redwood will deliver the labeling UI by 2026-10-14 as previously proposed. (Action: Ben)

2) Refund Extraction MOPs: Accept revised initial recall 78% for go/no-go. We will run a staged acceptance: initial acceptance at 78% during joint eval, plus a 4-week optimization window post-eval with target >=82%. If after the optimization window we do not reach 82% we will discuss mitigation (model tweak, expanded sample).

3) Timeline: Noted Procurement needs +1 week. Updated milestones below:
- Amendment signed: 2026-10-19 (Azura)
- Redwood deliver eval harness + labeling UI: 2026-10-14 (Ben)
- Azura deliver 5k labeled sample + 10k raw transcripts (stratified): 2026-10-28 (Alex)
- Joint evaluation window: 2026-10-29 -> 2026-11-12
4) Contracts / amendment: I created a short amendment in DocuSign and linked it here: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/amendment-AZ-2026-019 — Alex / Procurement, please e-sign when you have legal sign-off.

If that looks good I can draft a one-page success tracker (we'll use the MOP spreadsheet to populate it) and route for signatures. Karthik — looping you for SLA ops and to confirm Dedicated sizing for the test window.

On the question of cost impact, we'll keep the incremental token delta to target <=12% as long as we keep the Dedicated config and use the KV cache for longer conversation prefixes.

Cheers,
Ben
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
